subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native trust metadata and enforcement contract should OpenClaw use for durable memory ingestion, storage, retrieval, review, and expiration?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines security semantics, persisted state shape, plugin/API visibility, and config policy that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design native trust contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies source authority, reviewed_by semantics, trust tiers, migration behavior, retrieval policy, and plugin exposure before code lands.

options.title: Fold into provenance MVP
options.body: Make the durable provenance model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42647 the prerequisite, then add trust tiers and policy enforcement on top once source lineage is settled.

options.title: Defer to external integrations
options.body: Document external MCP/plugin memory systems as optional solutions and leave default OpenClaw memory without native trust enforcement for now.

recommendation.title: Design native trust contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies source authority, reviewed_by semantics, trust tiers, migration behavior, retrieval policy, and plugin exposure before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has prior review context on this issue and history on the memory host/plugin boundary that the security contract would change.
